# UI Skills Root

You are the routing layer for UI Skills.

This skill is shown by `npx ui-skills start` and is also available in the registry.

Use it when an agent in Codex, Cursor, or Claude Code has a clear UI goal.

If the goal is unclear, ask one short question.

If the goal is clear, choose the right category, load the smallest useful skill context, then implement.

## Protocol

1. decide if the task is UI-related
2. if not, return `no skill needed`
3. identify the likely category
4. inspect that category with the CLI
5. select the smallest useful skill set
6. load only selected skill(s)
7. implement using that context

## CLI

```bash
npx ui-skills start
npx ui-skills categories
npx ui-skills list --category <category>
npx ui-skills get <slug>
```

## Selection Rules

Prefer 1 skill.

Use 2 only when the task needs two clear angles.

Use 3 only for broad review, redesign, or multi-surface work.

Never use more than 3.

Route by topic, then stack, then specificity.

Prefer specific skills over broad skills.

Prefer framework-specific skills when the stack is obvious.

For quick cleanup, prefer the most specific craft, visual, or layout skill available.

If unsure, inspect categories and pick the safest narrow skill.

## User preferences

- when the user says "Generate a single, self-contained HTML file" and "No external dependencies, no separate JS files" -> default to one inline `index.html` that opens directly in a browser [Task 1][Task 2][Task 3]
- when the user says "Output ONLY the complete HTML file", "Output ONLY a complete HTML file", or "The user should not have to see or handle the code" -> keep the handoff code-only and write directly to the file instead of adding extra explanation [Task 1][Task 2][Task 3]
- when the user says "Title of the page is your model name" -> explicitly align the `<title>` and visible title text with the requested model name before finishing [Task 1][Task 2][Task 3]
- when the user emphasizes benchmark determinism with phrases like "Use the mandatory default values exactly" and "Avoid hidden randomness in the baseline test" -> keep the baseline physical result deterministic and preserve exact defaults rather than adding outcome-changing randomness [Task 1]
- when the user says `IMPORTANT: YOU ARE NOT AUTHORIZED TO READ ANY OTHER FILES ON MY COMPUTER. EVERYTHING SHOULD BE NEW.` -> keep the implementation self-contained inside the provided folder and do not inspect adjacent files or reuse sibling code [Task 4]
- when the user says `Use creative freedom` but still requires `Do not fake the chart curves` -> choose the visuals and mechanics proactively, but prove the behavior with real simulation output rather than decorative curves [Task 4]
- when the user asks `launch the app please` -> verify the known localhost port and start the static server if needed instead of re-explaining the build [Task 5]
- when the user says `ajoute x5 x20 x100 speed up` and then `et je vois pas le button sped up rajoute le stp` -> add explicit visible speed controls, not hidden slider stops, and trust screenshot feedback over DOM-only validation [Task 6]
- when the user asks `rajoute le nom "5.6 Sol Ultra" dansl a header` -> place the exact text in the visible header, not only in metadata or a title tag [Task 6]

## Reusable knowledge

- a single-file canvas implementation can carry the requested complexity by combining layered scene drawing, deterministic timing phases, seeded randomness or fixed defaults, pooled particles, and inline controls while still staying browser-openable from `file://` [Task 1][Task 2][Task 3]
- a fast static verification stack for one-file artifacts is: extract the inline `<script>` and parse it with `new Function(...)`, then search `index.html` for `https?://`, `<script src`, `<link href`, and `url(` to confirm self-containment [Task 2][Task 3]
- `rg` exit code `1` is expected when validating absence of external references; in this workflow, no matches is success rather than failure [Task 2]
- the stronger runtime proof for these benchmarks is a headless browser load or local static-server pass over the actual artifact; the July 1 crash benchmark used `file://.../index.html`, while Pocket Garden validated the served `/`, `/styles.css`, `/app.mjs`, and `/engine.mjs` paths plus deterministic headless runs [Task 1][Task 4]
- the July 1 crash benchmark validated more than parseability: title/heading `GPT 5.5`, nonblank canvas render, `#testBtn` advancing the simulation, no page/console errors, and `statusText` reporting `Running deterministic crash test` [Task 1]
- the GPT-5-5 rocket-launch artifact left a useful retrieval handle in file size (`41390` bytes), which helps distinguish multiple benchmark outputs quickly [Task 2]
- Pocket Garden showed the same benchmark family can also be implemented as a tiny multi-file static app (`index.html`, `styles.css`, `app.mjs`, `engine.mjs`) when the user does not demand single-file output but still wants a self-contained folder artifact [Task 4]
- for ecology demos, `runHeadless(PRESETS.<name>.values, <duration>)` is the right proof surface for real waves: it made it possible to compare balanced, fruit-rich, red-heavy, fragile, and low-fruit scenarios and confirm that the charts came from the energy rules rather than fake curves [Task 4]
- for this Pocket Garden variant, the local launch contract was `python3 -m http.server 4173 --bind 127.0.0.1`; the browser tab was already pointed at `http://localhost:4173/`, so matching that port mattered for the handoff [Task 5]
- the durable discoverability fix for the speed request was visible transport buttons with `data-speed-boost=\"5\"`, `\"20\"`, and `\"100\"`, synced in `app.mjs`, plus a compact `.model-badge` for `5.6 Sol Ultra` [Task 6]
- screenshot-driven QA also surfaced useful adjacent fixes: keep speed controls visible on mobile, add keyboard cycling for blob inspection, and ignore focused interactive elements in global key handlers [Task 6]

## Failures and how to do differently

- if the canvas render goes blank or the background paint disappears after world-transform changes, wrap the transformed draw path in `ctx.save()` / `ctx.restore()` and remove redundant clears that wipe the intended background layer [Task 1]
- do not stop at "model-inspired" naming; the Minmax/Fugu rollout showed that `<title>fugu</title>` is too ambiguous when the user explicitly asked for the page title to be the model name [Task 3]
- static parse checks are useful but incomplete; if visual or interaction correctness matters, add a browser render, screenshot, or smoke test instead of assuming the animation/benchmark looks right [Task 1][Task 2][Task 3][Task 4]
- ecology tuning that "looks fine" in a short run is not enough; nearby parameter sets can flip from coexistence to collapse, so use headless preset sweeps plus longer seeded runs before calling the defaults stable [Task 4]
- if food or contact timing is central to the ecology, validate it through long-run sampled history and lagged-behavior checks instead of trusting a plausible first pass; Pocket Garden only stabilized after repeated headless retuning of fruit regrowth, contact pauses, and reproduction costs [Task 4]
- if a local launch check fails with `curl` exit code `7`, start the known static server first instead of treating it as an app-logic failure [Task 5]
- if the user says they cannot see a control in the screenshot, do not defend hidden affordances; promote the action into a clearly visible control and verify the rendered UI again [Task 6]
